title: Density-aware metric cards — keyboard microflows & localized number truncation a11y review
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Dense metric cards in the Console (cost + perf dashboards) currently trade legibility for information density. In compact layouts we collapse labels and use abbreviation heuristics (e.g., 1.2K), but this breaks localization rules (some locales use non-breaking spaces, different grouping, or different units) and keyboard focus order is inconsistent when cards collapse. Goal: define an accessible, locale-aware truncation strategy and keyboard microflows for dense metric cards that preserves keyboard discoverability, screen reader friendliness, and high contrast support. Deliverables: 1) a design spec with acceptance criteria and visual tokens for a contrast-safe compact palette; 2) an annotated prototype demonstrating keyboard flows for both expanded and compact states; 3) i18n rules for number formatting/fallbacks; 4) implementation notes for Eng (aria attributes, focus management, CSS tokens).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compact cards show unambiguous value presentation for top 3 locales (en-US, fr-FR, hi-IN) without visual overflow.
- Keyboard tab order is predictable: container > primary metric > actions menu > overflow details.
- Screen reader announces: {metric-name}, {localized-value}, {trend-label}.
- High-contrast token set meets 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for UI control labels in compact mode.
- Fallback when space is constrained: tooltip on hover and accessible disclosure on Enter/Space.
- Engineering has a single aria pattern and CSS token mapping to plug into runtime-1.22 rollout.
comments: 2025-10-13 — Asha: Initial hypothesis and mockups uploaded to Figma (link below). Proposed two truncation strategies: semantic truncation (round to unit + localized suffix) and precision clipping (fixed digits with localized separators).

2025-10-16 — UX Research (Miguel Ortega): Micro-usability session (n=6) shows users misread metric suffixes in fr-FR when using thin spacing; suggested non-breaking thin-space and explicit unit labels where ambiguity exists.

2025-10-20 — Accessibility review (Priya Shah): flagged screen reader announcements — recommended using aria-labelledby combining hidden label elements rather than relying on innerText. Also recommended role="group" on the card with aria-roledescription for density mode.

2025-10-25 — Engineering sync (Jonas Meyer): advised against complex JS locale formatting on the critical render path; prefer server-prepared localized strings with a client-side fallback. Also requested concrete aria attributes to implement (provided in Implementation Notes).

2025-10-28 — Design update: Introduced Contrast Ivory token set (primary: #0B1220 on ivory #FCFBF8) for compact cards to preserve information hierarchy. Ran automated contrast checks; body and primary values pass 4.8:1.
2025-10-30 — PM check-in (Riley Chen): ask to include RTL behavior verification and to add a follow-up engineering task for telemetry to see how often tooltips are used for truncated values.
2025-11-01 — Designer handoff ready — exported annotated prototype, updated acceptance criteria, and created engineering spec stub. Moving to In Review.
implementation_notes:
- Keyboard flow: Tab lands on card container. Pressing Enter expands inline disclosure (aria-expanded). Arrow keys move focus between elements inside an expanded card. Escape collapses disclosure and returns focus to card.
- Screen reader: use aria-labelledby for metric name and value, aria-describedby for trend text. Provide data-unit as data-* attribute for analytics.
- i18n: prefer Intl.NumberFormat on server when possible; client fallback uses locale table: {"en-US":"compact-suffix-K/M","fr-FR":"space-grouping","hi-IN":"lakh-crore"} (engineering to canonicalize map).
- Visual tokens: provide contrast-ivory set and compact spacing utility. Avoid using gradient backgrounds in compact mode to keep edge contrast deterministic.
- Performance: avoid layout shifts — render disclosure offscreen and reveal with opacity where possible.
next_steps:
- Collect RTL screenshots and run automated contrast checks for all supported locales.
- Create ENG ticket for server-side localized formatting fallback and telemetry.
- Schedule accessibility QA with Priya (a11y engineer) and 2 devs for implementation review.
- Ship prototype to product managers for prioritization in the console-2025.11 release cadence.
